title: Exploring Magnets

key_big: Like poles repel; unlike poles attract.
key_sub: A freely hanging magnet points north–south.
body_html:
How to think about it

A magnet attracts magnetic materials such as iron, nickel and cobalt, but not wood, plastic, glass, copper or aluminium. Its attraction is strongest at its two poles. A freely hanging magnet always comes to rest pointing north–south; a compass uses this to show directions.

Like poles repel and unlike poles attract, so repulsion is the surest test of a magnet. An iron nail can be made into a magnet by stroking it in one direction with a magnet. Heating, hammering and dropping make magnets weak, so store them in pairs with keepers.

Example

North pole near north pole?

like poles

Answer: they repel

Example

Is a copper wire attracted by a magnet?

copper is not magnetic

Answer: no

Common mistakes

  • Thinking a magnet attracts all metals.
  • Thinking attraction proves an object is a magnet.
  • Saying a broken magnet has only one pole in each piece.

faq.a: Iron is attracted to a magnet too, but only another magnet can be repelled by it.
